Kento Alpha 0.9.38, build 2998

New

  • VectorRetime's motion blur: shutterSamples and shutterTime now blur the retimed picture, the samples spread evenly over the shutter around each frame and weighted equally, as Nuke renders it.
  • LightKey's alpha bias and despill bias now work, as do the None and Source replace methods with a clip, matching Nuke.

Fixes

  • A movie with a sound track played a frame late inside each run of frames Kento decoded together.
  • A Read set to black before or after its range gave a picture with no channels, so a TimeClip, AppendClip or Keymix past a clip's end had nothing to show. It now gives black with the file's channels.
  • A Bento made from a group with its own controls, such as a transition, lost their values and played as if at the defaults.
  • Matched to Nuke's renders: Copy where A reaches past B, VectorCornerPin between its keys, Stabilize2D's scale factor, TimeClip reversed, TimeOffset's whole frames for negative offsets, CheckerBoard2 on non-square pixels, HSVTool on pixels outside 0 to 1, and AddMix outside A.

Kento Alpha 0.9.37, build 2979

New

  • Create LUT, Kento's own node for making a LUT from what the comp does to color (Color > Create LUT). Put it at the end of the nodes to bake: everything between start at and here becomes one LUT, branches that split and join again included, each node switchable out. A node a LUT can't hold (a blur, a mask that changes across the frame) is found, left out and named. Or make it from a Match Grade, or from a test pattern graded in another app.
  • Create LUT opens simple: made for chooses what the LUT is for (the grade for Resolve, a viewing LUT for editorial, an on-set monitor, OCIO apps) and sets the color spaces, shaper, size and format together. One sentence says what Write LUT will make, and after writing, the check says in plain words how close the file is to the nodes. All options, in the header, shows every option; changing one by hand says what changed, with Back to the use you chose, and a risky combination is named with a button that fixes it.
  • Create LUT writes .cube in Resolve's style, CLF, plain .cube and CTF. With CLF or CTF a single chain of pure color transforms is written as those operations, with no table, checked against the nodes first.
  • Startup scripts in Settings > Scripting: Nuke-style init.py and menu.py folders and files, their menus in the Scripts menu, knob defaults, formats, gizmo folders and callbacks. A menu key Kento already uses stays Kento's, and the card offers a free key near it.
  • Startup scripts' callbacks for a node class run: nuke.addKnobChanged as you set a control on a node of that class (a Read's file, say) and as its panel opens, and nuke.addOnDestroy as a node is deleted.
  • Settings > AI and MCP, a page of its own: Connect an assistant lists the AI apps found on this Mac, local-model ones too, and sets one up to drive Kento.
  • A gizmo whose scripts only show, hide or set controls becomes a Bento like any other.

Fixes

  • Matched to NukeX 17.1's renders: LightKey's screen gain, Radial at softness 0 (a one-pixel soft edge, not a hard one), DeepFromFrames' frames, depths and premult, LensDistortion2's Height normalization, and how Reformat and Transform round each filter's position.
  • Flare with a visibility mask was cut off where the mask's input stopped.
  • bm_CameraShake crashed Kento.
  • A transition made into a Bento stopped working.

Kento Alpha 0.9.36, build 2922

New

  • File > Add to this comp... brings another comp's nodes (a .nk or a .ko) into the comp in front, beside what's there, as one undo. The open comp keeps its own range, format and frame rate, and says where the added comp's differed; footage paths are made absolute so they still find their files.
  • Copy and paste with Nuke and between Kento windows. Copy puts the selected nodes on the system clipboard as Nuke script text and as Kento's own copy; Paste reads nodes copied in Nuke, or in another Kento, with Kento's readers.
  • Python in comps and gizmos runs, as in Nuke. A gizmo's onCreate, its knobChanged as its panel opens and whenever a control changes, and its Python buttons all run, through Kento's stand-in for Nuke's Python module; what a control's change does through its script comes off with it in one undo. A gizmo whose script rebuilds its inside when a control changes does so here too, and its text lines, dividers and buttons hide and dim as its script says.
  • A comp's own callbacks run: onScriptLoad as a Nuke script opens, onScriptSave before it's saved as one, and the comp's and each Write's before and after render and frame callbacks in the Render window, the Render Queue and command-line renders.
  • Before any script runs, Kento reads it. One that reaches files, the shell or the network still runs, and a card in the window's corner shows the lines and why. Don't warn about this script again trusts it from then on. Settings > Scripting can ask before such a script runs instead (off by default).
  • Scripts can read bounding boxes (a node's bbox, as in Nuke), run a CurveTool's analysis, and use Nuke's AutoCrop, which keys a Crop to the picture over the comp's range.
  • Kento's own Python module for scripts, tools and batches: import kento in the Script Editor, a startup script or Kento's Python without the interface. Comps, nodes and knobs by Nuke's names, keys at frames, one undo for a block of changes; every remote control command from a script; the Viewer (show a node, its look, its wipe); callbacks when comps open and close, the frame changes or nodes are added; and a stub file so code editors complete the calls.
  • Kiri's Balance: Match to background sets exposure, contrast, warmth and tint part of the way toward the plate behind, each with a lock, and light wrap brings the background's light around the edges.
  • Kiri's checking views, in its row over the Viewer: Result, Matte, Bands, Spill and Foreground.
  • Kiri's kept colors: pick colors the despill leaves alone (a green costume, a plant) with the dropper; a pixel near a kept color keeps its own color at any brightness.

Fixes

  • Setting a box control from a script with four numbers set both corners to the first number.
  • A gizmo's scripts read as written in the Nuke script: before, they could look as if they had nothing to do.
